title: Asking How Many : いくつ / 何～

blocks.content: There are two ways to ask "how many" in Japanese. Use **いくつ** when the category is unspecified or you want a general count. Use **何** (なん) directly before the counter when the category is already known.

left.label: いくつ
left.description: General count : used when the category is unspecified, or for things without a fixed counter.
left.example_jp: りんごがいくつありますか。

right.label: 何 + counter
right.description: Category-specific : attach 何 (nan) directly before the counter you would normally use.

rows.english: How many books did you read?

blocks.content: いくつ is also used informally to ask someone's age : お子さんはいくつですか (How old is your child?). The direct "how old" question is 何歳 (nansai).
